blocks.html: A shot at seeing the Mara River crossing, then on to Zanzibar by air

blocks.orig: This is a special trip, as it takes you past two wonders of nature and into a safari plane! First, you drive to Tarangire National Park (baobabs and elephants!), and then on to the famous Ngorongoro crater – the first wonder! From there, you journey on to the northern part of Serengeti National Park where, with a bit of luck, you catch the famous Mara River crossing (the second wonder!), which occurs yearly from late July to early October.
blocks.html: This trip is a special one: it brings you to two natural wonders and onto a safari plane! You begin by driving to Tarangire National Park (baobabs and elephants!) and continue to the famous Ngorongoro crater, which is the first wonder. Next you travel on to the northern Serengeti National Park, where with a little luck you see the famous Mara River crossing (wonder number two!), which takes place every year from late July to early October.

blocks.orig: Imagine seeing thousands of wildebeests and zebras together in a herd, all moaning and braying in their distinctive sounds, kicking up dust and protecting each other from the surrounding predators. This Great Wildebeest Migration, and especially the Mara River crossing, is an amazing and thrilling spectacle to witness, as the river is full of crocodiles lurking at all that meat crossing their waters… Can you feel the thrill?
blocks.html: Picture thousands of wildebeests and zebras moving together in one herd, moaning and braying in their typical way, raising clouds of dust and guarding one another against the predators all around. Watching this Great Wildebeest Migration, and above all the Mara River crossing, is an amazing and exciting experience, because the river is full of crocodiles waiting for all that meat coming through their waters… Do you feel the excitement?

blocks.orig: And just when the excitement is getting too much, we load you onto a safari plane and take you straight to the magic of Zanzibar – looong sigh! – where you can relax on a quiet, tropical beach…
blocks.html: And right when the thrill starts to become too much, we put you on a safari plane and fly you directly to magical Zanzibar – looong sigh! – where a quiet tropical beach is waiting for you to unwind…

blocks.orig: Many travelers ask us when the best time is to visit Tanzania. The answer is … there is not one right answer. It depends on what you want to see, where you want to go, your budget and interests. Please find a comprehensive guide on when is the best time to visit Tanzania here.
blocks.html: Lots of travellers want to know which time of year is best for Tanzania. Honestly, no single answer fits everyone. It comes down to what you hope to see, where you would like to go, and your interests and budget. You can read our detailed guide on the best time to visit Tanzania here.

blocks.orig: Our safaris in Tanzania offer an opportunity to explore the country’s incredible wildlife and stunning landscapes. We specialize in private safaris, which means you have a 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep all to yourselves. You have the flexibility to decide when the safari starts and ends, and our experienced guides can help you make that decision on the day of your adventure. Whether you want to witness the animals at their most active during sunrise and sunset when temperatures are pleasant, or if you fancy ending the day by the pool, it’s entirely up to you. Tanzania’s diverse wildlife is active at various times of the day, so you’ll have plenty of opportunities to spot the animals in action.
blocks.html: With our Tanzania safaris you get the chance to discover the country’s remarkable wildlife and beautiful scenery. Private safaris are our speciality: the 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep is yours alone. You choose when each safari day begins and finishes, and on the day itself our experienced guides are happy to help you decide. Perhaps you would like to catch the animals at their busiest around sunrise and sunset, when it is pleasantly cool, or you’d rather round off the day at the pool; it’s your call. Because Tanzania’s wildlife is active at different moments throughout the day, you will have lots of chances to watch animals in action.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is renowned as one of the prime destinations to encounter the Big Five. These magnificent creatures—lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros, and buffalo—can be observed in their natural habitats, making Tanzania a preferred choice for wildlife enthusiasts.
blocks.html: Yes, definitely. Tanzania is known as one of the top destinations for meeting the Big Five. Lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros and buffalo can all be seen here in their natural surroundings, which is why so many wildlife lovers choose Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is a safe and welcoming destination for travelers. The country offers a hospitable environment, especially in tourist areas like Arusha, and you can explore its beautiful landscapes and wildlife with confidence. Local people are friendly, and safety measures, such as keeping an eye on your belongings, are always advisable, just as you would in any other part of the world. Tanzania’s natural beauty and the warmth of its people make it a fantastic place to visit.
blocks.html: Yes, Tanzania is a safe and friendly country to travel in. The atmosphere is hospitable, particularly in tourist areas such as Arusha, so you can enjoy the scenery and wildlife with peace of mind. People are welcoming, and as anywhere else in the world it is sensible to take ordinary precautions, like keeping an eye on your belongings. Thanks to Tanzania’s natural beauty and its warm, welcoming people, it is a wonderful place to visit.

The next day your guide takes you on an exclusive, private safari that allows you to travel at your own pace. blocks.html: Once you step out of Kilimanjaro International Airport, your own Your Tanzania Trip guide welcomes you with a broad smile: 'Karibu Tanzania - welcome to Tanzania!' You are driven directly to your hotel to unwind and soak up the African atmosphere. The following day your guide sets off with you on an exclusive private safari, so you can travel at whatever pace suits you. blocks.orig: Tarangire National Park is well known for its big groups of elephants and the huge amount of giant baobab trees. These trees can live for hundreds of years and are actually a source of water for elephants in the dry season as they have a special technique to draw water from them. Besides, the Tarangire River is the only source of water in the dry season, which is why in this season in Tarangire you can see groups of up to 250 elephants next to many more animals!
blocks.html: Tarangire National Park is famous for its large herds of elephants and its great number of giant baobab trees. These baobabs can reach an age of several hundred years, and in the dry season they even supply elephants with water, as the elephants have a special way of extracting it from the trees. On top of that, the Tarangire River is the only water source during the dry season, so at that time of year you can find herds of up to 250 elephants in Tarangire, along with many other animals!

blocks.orig: The famous Ngorongoro Crater is one of Africa's seven natural wonders. The crater was formed two million years ago when a vast volcano erupted. The fertile lava has created a unique ecosystem, now home to the highest concentration of animals found anywhere in Africa! Once in the crater, thousands of animals such as lions, zebras, buffalos and black rhinos surround you, and the views are astounding – you won’t know where to look!
blocks.html: The well-known Ngorongoro Crater counts as one of Africa's seven natural wonders. It came into being two million years ago, when an enormous volcano erupted. The fertile lava gave rise to a unique ecosystem, which today holds the highest concentration of animals anywhere in Africa! Down in the crater you are surrounded by thousands of animals, including lions, zebras, buffalos and black rhinos, and the scenery is so astonishing that you won’t know which way to look!

blocks.orig: Serengeti National Park is widely known as the place to go on safari, mainly because of the Great Migration that passes through here. The enormous, stampeding herds are impressive, as are the vast number of predators that live here: over four thousand lions, over 200 cheetahs, a thousand leopards, 3500 hyenas, and hundreds of wild dogs! And of course, plenty of other beautiful animals, which your guide will be delighted to search for together with you. Are you ready for this?
blocks.html: Many people see Serengeti National Park as the safari destination, largely thanks to the Great Migration that moves through the park. The huge, thundering herds are a sight to behold, and so is the large number of predators living here: more than four thousand lions, over 200 cheetahs, a thousand leopards, 3500 hyenas and hundreds of wild dogs! There are also plenty of other beautiful animals, and your guide will be glad to go looking for them with you. Are you ready?

blocks.orig: Imagine crossing the grassy plains of northern Serengeti with your guide, and coming across millions of wildebeests and zebras, moaning and bleating as they attempt to cross a river full of crocodiles. This is the famous Mara River crossing of the Great Migration, a natural wonder that every year between July and October can be witnessed in the northern part of Serengeti National Park. This will be a nerve-racking event to watch - for did we mention the big cats waiting on the other side, just as hungry for meat as the herds are for greener pastures...?
blocks.html: Imagine you and your guide out on the grass-covered plains of the northern Serengeti, when you suddenly come upon millions of zebras and wildebeests, bleating and moaning while they attempt to get across a crocodile-infested river. What you are seeing is the well-known Mara River crossing, part of the Great Migration: a natural wonder that happens in the northern part of Serengeti National Park every year from July to October. It is a nail-biting moment to witness - because have we told you about the big cats lying in wait on the far bank, just as eager for a meal as the herds are for greener grass...?

blocks.orig: Today you fly to the spice island of Zanzibar. Our guide picks you up at the airport and takes you to your hotel. Over the next few days, you can discover white sandy beaches, crystal-clear turquoise waters and vibrant coral reefs. Into culture? Then head to Stone Town and dive into the history of this fascinating little town. Food lovers can also visit the spice plantations and discover the diverse flavours of the delicious local cuisine. A tropical paradise awaits you!
blocks.html: Today you take a flight to Zanzibar, the spice island. At the airport our guide meets you and brings you to your hotel. In the days that follow, you can explore white sandy beaches, clear turquoise water and colourful coral reefs. Interested in culture? Make your way to Stone Town and immerse yourself in the history of this fascinating small town. If you love food, you can also visit the spice plantations and get to know the many flavours of the delicious local cuisine. A tropical paradise is waiting for you!

blocks.orig: Ultimate paradise is here: gorgeous, tropical Zanzibar! The clear blue waters of the Indian Ocean and the palm-fringed, white sandy beaches are almost too beautiful to be true. Buy your coconut drink fresh on the beach, spend hours sunbathing or swimming, and taste the delicious Zanzibari food. In the mood for something active? Then explore the beach, ocean, and island through a range of activities! We highly recommend the Safari Blue Cruise or a tour of Stone Town.
blocks.html: Welcome to paradise: beautiful, tropical Zanzibar! With the clear blue water of the Indian Ocean and its white sandy beaches lined with palm trees, it almost seems too good to be real. Pick up a fresh coconut drink on the beach, sunbathe or swim for hours, and sample the tasty Zanzibari food. Feel like doing something active? Then discover the beach, the ocean and the island with a variety of activities! Our strong tip: the Safari Blue Cruise or a tour of Stone Town.

blocks.orig: The last day! Depending on your flight time, you can relax on the beach or explore the island just a little bit more. Then, make your way to Zanzibar International Airport in time for your flight home. Having second thoughts? It's also possible to extend your holiday to another paradise island, such as Mnemba, Pemba, or Mafia!
blocks.html: Your final day! Depending on when your flight leaves, you can unwind on the beach or see a little more of the island. After that, you travel to Zanzibar International Airport in time for your flight home. Not quite ready to leave? You can also extend your holiday on another paradise island, for example Mnemba, Pemba or Mafia!
